connector: In Chapter 11, the story follows Edmund on the Witch's sledge. It is a long, cold ride. Then he hears a sound he has not heard in Narnia before: running water. Watch what happens to the snow, and what it might stand for.

a.raw: the witchs dwarf couldnt make the sledge move
a.fixed: The Witch’s dwarf couldn’t make the sledge move.
a.why: The begins the sentence. Witch’s shows the dwarf works for her. Couldn’t joins could and not.

b.raw: edmund didnt want the dry bread but he ate it
b.fixed: Edmund didn’t want the dry bread, but he ate it.
b.why: Edmund is a name. Didn’t joins did and not. A comma goes before but.

cards.title: World Notes: Spring Flowers
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapter with your lens in mind.
text: Snowdrops are often the first flowers of the year. They can push up while snow is still on the ground.
Celandines are small yellow flowers. They open in sunshine and close up when it turns cloudy.
Crocuses come up in late winter and early spring, in purple, white and gold. Edmund sees all three as the snow melts.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. Edmund rides with the Witch, and then he hears running water. Watch what happens to the snow in Chapter 11.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: match together words, find what each apostrophe does, and spot endings that change a word.
transcripts.guide2: Read Chapter 11. Then watch my video in Read Like a Writer.
transcripts.guide3: Today you make your symbol paragraph more precise.

notes.wordParts: The word parts com- and con- both mean with or together. combine = to join together. connect = to tie together.
notes.grammar: An apostrophe has two jobs. It joins two words: did + not = didn’t. It shows belonging: Lucy’s bottle is the bottle that belongs to Lucy.
notes.spelling: Some endings change the base word. Double the last letter: run → running. Drop the silent e: hope → hoping. Change y to i: carry → carried.
notes.wgrd: The snow has been in every chapter. In Chapter 11 it melts. The thaw stands for the Witch's power breaking.
vocab: made new again; restored to a fresh state
a person or thing that announces something important is coming
cheerful and friendly; in high spirits

mods.label: Opti shows you how
mods.script: Let's try all three parts with a sentence from Chapter 11. The snow was again falling as they came into the courtyard, but she took no notice of that and made Edmund sit beside her on the sledge. Part one, read like a reader. The Witch doesn't care about the snow. Part two, read like a writer. Weather first, then but turns to the story. Part three, mimic. Here's mine: The rain was pouring as we left school, but Mom took no notice and made us run to the car. Now it's your turn with the sentence about the snow and the moon. Write one sentence in each box.

mods.todo: Answer each question in full sentences. Use details from the book.
mods.script: Three questions, in full sentences. One, how the Witch acts when the snow melts. Two, one thing that keeps coming back, and what it stands for. Three, how Edmund has changed by the end of Chapter 11.

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: The Witch gives Edmund dry bread instead of the Turkish Delight she promised him.
items.why: She does not keep her promise.

items.t: A little squirrel says Father Christmas really did come, even when the Witch says to call it a lie.
items.why: He tells the truth, even though the Witch is angry.

items.t: Edmund starts to see that the things he told himself about the Witch being good sound silly now.
items.why: He is finally being honest with himself.
